# The question

P.Oxy. 5292 preserves twelve intact trimeters of Sophocles' *Tereus* and
seventeen damaged ones (vv. 13–29). The judge-steered Markov walk restores
the seventeen verses together, as one passage: Stoicheia proposes a word,
the formal rules filter it, and an LLM judge (Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507)
decides by Metropolis–Hastings whether the passage reads better, its
log-odds taken to the power $1/T_{\text{judge}} = 4$. Sixteen chains start
from Eric Cullhed's eight reconstructions, two from each: eight run 12,000
steps and eight 10,000, and a state is kept every ten steps after a burn-in
of 300. (The data also hold sixteen chains under the smaller judge
Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, the set `chains_judge72_t4_v3e`, a short pilot
under Claude Sonnet 5.5, and eight more chains under the same judge from
starts unrelated to one another; this report reads one set, named by its
parameter `chain_set`, and sets the other sets beside it in the checks at
the end.) Which topics do the imputations put into the lost passage, and
does that differ from what Sophocles writes elsewhere?
(W. B. Henry's restoration of the same verses is in the data, but a single
text is not compared with the mean of thousands: it is left out.)

# The model

Every lemma of the vocabulary belongs to exactly one of $K$ semantic clusters
(word2vec on the lemmatised Greek corpus, Ward's method, cut at $K = 40$; two
rare-lemma clusters and four function-word clusters dropped, leaving 34).
Each cluster is named by the English glosses of the three lemmata nearest
its centre, for example *fine-word-matter* or *ship-sail-hull*. A
**document** is one whole restoration of the seventeen verses: all its
topic-bearing lemmata, however many there are, with nothing
cut off. Its topic counts are

$$\mathbf n \mid \theta \sim \mathrm{Multinomial}(N, \theta), \qquad
  \theta \sim \mathrm{Dirichlet}(\kappa \mathbf m),$$

where $N$ is the document's own length, $\mathbf m$ is the topic profile of
Sophocles' extant trimeters and $\kappa = 1$ is one pseudo-lemma's worth of
it. The prior says that a restoration is, a priori, Sophoclean, and it is
weak: with $\kappa = 1$ a document of twenty lemmata is 95 % data. A
symmetric prior would not do here, because documents differ in length and
a symmetric prior pulls short documents harder towards the uniform
profile, which fabricates lift for topics that are simply absent. The
Dirichlet is conjugate to the multinomial, so the posterior is exact,

$$\theta \mid \mathbf n \sim \mathrm{Dirichlet}(\kappa \mathbf m + \mathbf n),$$

and needs no sampler beyond `rgamma`. Two sets of documents are compared:

- the **imputations**: every recorded state of the sixteen chains, one
  document each;
- **Sophocles**, the baseline: every window of seventeen consecutive extant
  trimeters of Sophocles, one document each, the same shape as the lacuna.

Two posteriors are read from each set. The posterior of a **random
document** is the equal mixture of the documents' posteriors: its spread is
the spread between restorations plus the Dirichlet uncertainty of each. The
posterior of the **mean profile** is the average of the documents'
posteriors, draw by draw: it says what the imputations put into the passage on
average, and with thousands of restorations it is sharp. The imputations are
compared with Sophocles on both levels:
$P(\bar\theta_k^{\text{imp}} > \bar\theta_k^{\text{Soph}})$ for the mean
profiles over paired draws, with the lift of the means, and
$P(\theta_k^{\text{doc}} > \theta_k^{\text{window}})$ for a random document
against a random window of Sophocles, which measures how much the two
populations overlap. A topic counts as **raised** when the mean-profile
probability is at least 0.9 and the lift at least 1.5. Only the restored
text enters a document:
the surviving letters of a damaged verse are never counted.

# Data

The dataset `Urdatorn/bsda-miniproject-2026` on the Hugging Face Hub: one bag
of content lemmata per restored verse, the vocabulary with its cluster labels,
and the corpus of the three tragedians. The three files (20 MB) are
downloaded into `data/` the first time the report is knitted.

```{r download, include = FALSE}
hub <- "https://huggingface.co/datasets/Urdatorn/bsda-miniproject-2026"
dir.create(params$data, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
for (file_name in c("vocab.json", "corpus.parquet", "imputations.parquet")) {
  local_path <- file.path(params$data, file_name)
  if (!file.exists(local_path)) {
    url <- paste(hub, "resolve/main", file_name, sep = "/")
    download.file(url, local_path, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
  }
}
```

```{r data}
vocab <- fromJSON(file.path(params$data, "vocab.json"))
corpus <- read_parquet(file.path(params$data, "corpus.parquet"))
imputations <- read_parquet(file.path(params$data, "imputations.parquet"))

# Every row of corpus and imputations is one bag of lemmata: the lemma
# indices (lemma_idx, counted from 0) and how often each occurs (count).
# This function turns a table of bags into one long vector of lemma indices,
# repeating each index as often as it was counted.
lemma_stream <- function(table) {
  indices <- unlist(table$lemma_idx)
  counts <- unlist(table$count)
  rep(indices, counts)
}

# A lemma index becomes the label of its topic. Lemmata without a topic (NA)
# are dropped: they are not observations of any topic.
topic_stream <- function(lemma_indices) {
  labels <- vocab$cluster_K40[lemma_indices + 1]   # R counts from 1
  labels[!is.na(labels)]
}

# The topics, ordered by how much of the tragic corpus they cover
tragedians <- c("sophocles", "aeschylus", "euripides")
tragic <- filter(corpus, source %in% tragedians)
tragic_topics <- topic_stream(lemma_stream(tragic))
topic_mass <- sort(table(tragic_topics), decreasing = TRUE)
topic_names <- names(topic_mass)
K <- length(topic_names)

cat(K, "topics;", nrow(vocab), "lemmata in the vocabulary,",
    sum(!is.na(vocab$cluster_K40)), "with a topic;",
    nrow(imputations), "restored verses\n")
```

# The topics

The 34 topics are hard clusters of the vocabulary, built upstream (word2vec
on the lemmatised Greek corpus, Ward's method, cut at $K = 40$, six clusters
dropped) and delivered with the vocabulary as `cluster_K40`; the Greek
triple behind each English label is the three lemmata nearest the cluster's
centre. The table orders them by their share of the three tragedians'
trimeters; the LaTeX version for the paper is `latex/topics_table.tex`.

```{r topics_table}
with_topic <- filter(vocab, !is.na(cluster_K40))
topics_table <- data.frame(topic = topic_names,
                           lemmata_greek = NA, lemmata = NA, tragic_tokens = NA)
for (i in seq_len(K)) {
  members <- filter(with_topic, cluster_K40 == topic_names[i])
  topics_table$lemmata_greek[i] <- members$cluster_K40_lemmata[1]
  topics_table$lemmata[i] <- nrow(members)
  topics_table$tragic_tokens[i] <- sum(members$tragic_count)
}
knitr::kable(topics_table, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("topic", "its three central lemmata", "lemmata",
                           "tragic tokens"))
```

The documents themselves: every imputation and every Sophoclean
window placed by UMAP from its profile over the 34 topics (Hellinger
distance), coloured by its dominant topic (`scripts/topic_map.py`).
Documents of a few dozen
lemmata are mixtures, so the map has no clean regions; it is for browsing
the restorations, not evidence.

```{r topic_map, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/hard_topic_map.png")
```

# The posterior

```{r model}
kappa <- params$kappa
draws <- params$draws

# One line per topic-bearing lemma of a table of bags, with the document
# (group) the lemma belongs to. `group` names the document of every row.
lemma_table <- function(table, group) {
  row_of_entry <- rep(seq_len(nrow(table)), lengths(table$lemma_idx))
  row_of_lemma <- rep(row_of_entry, unlist(table$count))
  lemmata <- data.frame(group = group[row_of_lemma],
                        topic = vocab$cluster_K40[lemma_stream(table) + 1])
  filter(lemmata, !is.na(topic))
}

# The documents of a table: the topic labels of every group, as a list.
# A group without any topic-bearing lemma gives no document.
make_documents <- function(table, group) {
  lemmata <- lemma_table(table, group)
  split(lemmata$topic, lemmata$group)
}

# S draws from a Dirichlet distribution: gamma variables, normalised to sum 1
rdirichlet <- function(S, parameters) {
  gammas <- matrix(rgamma(S * length(parameters), shape = parameters),
                   nrow = S, byrow = TRUE)
  gammas / rowSums(gammas)
}

# The prior: Sophocles' topic profile, worth kappa lemmata
sophocles_topics <- topic_stream(lemma_stream(filter(corpus,
                                                     source == "sophocles")))
prior_mean <- tabulate(match(sophocles_topics, topic_names), nbins = K)
prior_mean <- prior_mean / sum(prior_mean)
prior <- kappa * prior_mean

# The exact posterior of one document: count its labels per topic, add the
# prior, and draw from Dirichlet(prior + counts).
posterior_draws <- function(document) {
  counts <- tabulate(match(document, topic_names), nbins = K)
  rdirichlet(draws, prior + counts)
}

# The two posteriors of a set of documents. `document_draws` stacks the
# draws of all the documents: a random document. `mean_draws` averages the
# documents' draws, one average per draw index: the mean profile. If a
# baseline (Sophocles) is given, the set is compared with it on both
# levels, draw by draw.
summarise_documents <- function(documents, baseline = NULL) {
  n_docs <- length(documents)
  document_draws <- matrix(0, nrow = draws * n_docs, ncol = K)
  for (i in seq_len(n_docs)) {
    first <- (i - 1) * draws + 1
    last <- i * draws
    document_draws[first:last, ] <- posterior_draws(documents[[i]])
  }
  draw_index <- rep(seq_len(draws), times = n_docs)
  mean_draws <- rowsum(document_draws, draw_index) / n_docs
  result <- list(n_docs = n_docs,
                 n_lemmata = mean(lengths(documents)),
                 mean = colMeans(mean_draws),
                 q05 = apply(mean_draws, 2, quantile, probs = 0.05),
                 q95 = apply(mean_draws, 2, quantile, probs = 0.95),
                 document_draws = document_draws,
                 mean_draws = mean_draws)
  if (!is.null(baseline)) {
    result$p_above <- colMeans(mean_draws > baseline$mean_draws)
    result$lift <- colMeans(mean_draws) / colMeans(baseline$mean_draws)
    lift_draws <- mean_draws / baseline$mean_draws
    result$lift_q05 <- apply(lift_draws, 2, quantile, probs = 0.05)
    result$lift_q95 <- apply(lift_draws, 2, quantile, probs = 0.95)
    pick <- sample(nrow(baseline$document_draws), nrow(document_draws),
                   replace = TRUE)
    paired <- baseline$document_draws[pick, ]
    result$p_document <- colMeans(document_draws > paired)
  }
  result
}
```

The two sets of documents, and the model's table: one row per topic.

```{r documents}
# Sophocles' extant trimeters in windows of seventeen, the baseline
sophocles <- filter(corpus, source == "sophocles")
sophocles <- arrange(sophocles, line)
window <- (seq_len(nrow(sophocles)) - 1) %/% 17
sophocles_documents <- make_documents(sophocles, window)
baseline <- summarise_documents(sophocles_documents)

# Only untilted snapshots are used (the tilt flag is empty, NA, for the
# restorers that were never tilted)
untilted <- filter(imputations, !coalesce(style_tilted, FALSE))

# The imputations: the walk set named in the parameters, one document per
# snapshot (one chain at one step, all seventeen verses). Chains run alone
# have an empty chain number, so there the chain set is the chain.
imputations <- filter(untilted, restorer == "walk",
                      chain_set == params$chain_set)
stopifnot(nrow(imputations) > 0)
imputations$chain_id <- ifelse(is.na(imputations$chain), imputations$chain_set,
                        paste(imputations$chain_set, imputations$chain))
imputations$snapshot <- paste(imputations$chain_id, imputations$iteration)
imputation_documents <- make_documents(imputations, imputations$snapshot)
imputation_posterior <- summarise_documents(imputation_documents, baseline)

# One row per topic, the model's table
rows <- data.frame(topic = topic_names,
                   mean = imputation_posterior$mean,
                   q05 = imputation_posterior$q05,
                   q95 = imputation_posterior$q95,
                   p_above_sophocles = imputation_posterior$p_above,
                   lift = imputation_posterior$lift,
                   lift_q05 = imputation_posterior$lift_q05,
                   lift_q95 = imputation_posterior$lift_q95,
                   p_document = imputation_posterior$p_document)
rows$raised <- rows$p_above_sophocles >= 0.9 & rows$lift >= 1.5
for (column in c("mean", "q05", "q95", "p_above_sophocles", "lift",
                 "lift_q05", "lift_q95", "p_document")) {
  rows[[column]] <- round(rows[[column]], 4)
}

sizes <- data.frame(source = c("sophocles", "imputations"),
                    documents = c(baseline$n_docs, imputation_posterior$n_docs),
                    lemmata_per_document = c(baseline$n_lemmata,
                                             imputation_posterior$n_lemmata))
knitr::kable(sizes, digits = 1, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Documents, and topic-bearing lemmata per document")
```

# Sophocles' baseline

Sophocles' mean profile, the topics ordered by their share, each with its
posterior mean and 90 % interval on a log scale, so that the small
differences between topics can be read; the dashed line is the share every
topic would have if all were equal.

```{r baseline, fig.height = 5}
baseline_table <- data.frame(topic = reorder(topic_names, baseline$mean),
                             mean = baseline$mean,
                             q05 = baseline$q05,
                             q95 = baseline$q95)
ggplot(baseline_table, aes(x = mean, y = topic)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1 / length(topic_names), linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = q05, xmax = q95), colour = okabe_ito[["blue"]],
                  size = 0.25, linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "posterior mean of theta, with its 90 % interval (log scale)",
       y = NULL,
       title = paste("Sophocles,", baseline$n_docs,
                     "windows of seventeen trimeters"))
```

# Topics raised above Sophocles

Topics whose mean profile is above Sophocles' with
$P \ge 0.9$ and a lift of at least 1.5, with the lift, the posterior mean
and, in brackets, the document-level probability
$P(\theta_k^{\text{doc}} > \theta_k^{\text{window}})$.

```{r raised, results = "asis"}
raised <- arrange(filter(rows, raised), desc(lift))
if (nrow(raised) == 0) {
  cat("None.\n")
} else {
  items <- sprintf("%s (%.1f×, %.2f [%.2f])", raised$topic, raised$lift,
                   raised$mean, raised$p_document)
  cat(paste(items, collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
```

# Lift of every topic

The lift of every topic, ordered by lift, with its 90 % interval on a log
scale, where a lift of 2 and of 1/2 sit at the same distance from the
dashed line at 1.

```{r lifts, fig.height = 5}
lifts <- rows
lifts$topic <- reorder(lifts$topic, lifts$lift)
ggplot(lifts, aes(x = lift, y = topic, colour = raised)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lift_q05, xmax = lift_q95),
                  size = 0.25, linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey60", okabe_ito[["vermillion"]]),
                      name = "raised: P >= 0.9\nand lift >= 1.5") +
  labs(x = "lift of the mean profile against Sophocles (log scale)",
       y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# The largest lifts

The five topics with the largest lift.

```{r top}
top_five <- head(arrange(rows, desc(lift)), 5)
top_five <- top_five[, c("topic", "mean", "q05", "q95", "p_above_sophocles",
```

# Beyond Sophocles: three baselines

Is the imputations' profile unusual, and against whom? Two further baselines are
cut from other text into windows of 30 vocabulary lemmata, the length of
the imputations' mean document: Aeschylus and Euripides, and Classical Attic,
the works of the Attic authors before Alexander in the Open Greek and Latin
texts parsed by the same tagger (the tragedians with their lyrics,
Aristophanes, Thucydides, Xenophon, Plato, Aristotle, the Attic orators and
the sophists who wrote Attic, 23,328 windows). Sophocles is cut the same
way. The shares here are plain rates per thousand topic lemmata, pooled
over the documents of each set; a lift's 90 % interval comes from resampling the
imputations by chain and a baseline by window. The figures are drawn by
`scripts/topic_circles.py`, `scripts/topic_lemmata.py` and
`scripts/genre_distance.py` from `data/baseline_windows.parquet`
(`scripts/window_baselines.py`); their tables are in `results/hard/`.

One circle per topic, ordered by the imputations' share of it, coloured by the
log2 lift against each baseline, in full colour with the lift printed where
the interval excludes 1: against Sophocles, against Aeschylus and Euripides,
and against Classical Attic. The area runs from the smallest share to the
largest, since the shares of the 34 topics lie within a factor of two or
three of each other and circles proportional to the share itself would all
look alike.

```{r circles_imputations, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(c("figures/hard_circles_imputations_vs_sophocles.png",
                          "figures/hard_circles_imputations_vs_tragedians.png",
                          "figures/hard_circles_imputations_vs_attic.png"))
```

The same with Sophocles as the focus, against the other two tragedians and
against Classical Attic, so that his own topics are visible beside the
imputations':

```{r circles_sophocles, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(c("figures/hard_circles_sophocles_vs_tragedians.png",
                          "figures/hard_circles_sophocles_vs_attic.png"))
```

```{r baselines_table}
circles <- read.csv("results/hard/topic_circles.csv", encoding = "UTF-8")
circles$off_one <- circles$lift_q05 > 1 | circles$lift_q95 < 1
# For every comparison: how many topics have an interval off 1, and the
# three largest and three smallest lifts among them
baseline_rows <- NULL
for (comparison in unique(circles$comparison)) {
  these <- filter(circles, comparison == !!comparison, off_one)
  these <- arrange(these, desc(lift))
  largest <- paste(sprintf("%s %.2f", head(these$topic, 3),
                           head(these$lift, 3)), collapse = ", ")
  smallest <- paste(sprintf("%s %.2f", tail(these$topic, 3),
                            tail(these$lift, 3)), collapse = ", ")
  baseline_rows <- rbind(baseline_rows,
                         data.frame(comparison = comparison,
                                    off_one = nrow(these),
                                    largest = largest, smallest = smallest))
}
knitr::kable(baseline_rows, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("comparison", "topics off 1", "largest lifts",
                           "smallest lifts"))
```

The two lifts of every topic of the imputations side by side: against Sophocles
(the question of this report) and against Classical Attic (whether the
topic is tragic at all). A topic in the upper right is more frequent in
the imputations than in both; one on the dashed line at 1 is at its baseline's
rate. The dot is the imputations' mean share of the topic, the grey lines the
90 % intervals.

```{r lift_scatter, fig.height = 5.2}
against <- function(baseline) {
  rows <- filter(circles, comparison == paste("imputations vs", baseline))
  rows[, c("topic", "rate_focus", "lift", "lift_q05", "lift_q95")]
}
scatter <- inner_join(against("sophocles"), against("attic"),
                      by = c("topic", "rate_focus"),
                      suffix = c("_sophocles", "_attic"))
scatter$off_one <- scatter$lift_q05_sophocles > 1 |
  scatter$lift_q95_sophocles < 1 | scatter$lift_q05_attic > 1 |
  scatter$lift_q95_attic < 1
# every topic is labelled where ggrepel can keep the labels apart; without
# it, only the topics with an interval off 1 (the crowd at 1 stays unnamed)
labels <- if (requireNamespace("ggrepel", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = topic), size = 2,
                           family = figure_font, max.overlaps = Inf,
                           segment.size = 0.2, segment.colour = "grey60")
} else {
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(off_one, topic, "")), size = 2,
            vjust = -1.1, family = figure_font)
}
ggplot(scatter, aes(x = lift_attic, y = lift_sophocles)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lift_q05_sophocles, ymax = lift_q95_sophocles),
                 colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = lift_q05_attic, xmax = lift_q95_attic),
                 colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(size = rate_focus), colour = okabe_ito[["blue"]],
             alpha = 0.7) +
  labels +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(title = paste("The hard model: the imputations' lift against Sophocles",
                     "and Classical Attic"),
       x = "lift against Classical Attic (log scale)",
       y = "lift against Sophocles (log scale)",
       size = "mean share (%)")
```

Two lifts of the imputations hold against every baseline,
*wrong-vengeance-err* and *god-true-lord*. A third, *marriage-couch-bed*,
is raised against Sophocles and against Classical Attic but falls below
Aeschylus and Euripides, who use that vocabulary more than Sophocles does:

```{r held}
held <- filter(circles,
               topic %in% c("wrong-vengeance-err", "god-true-lord",
                            "marriage-couch-bed"),
               grepl("^imputations", comparison))
held <- held[, c("topic", "comparison", "lift", "lift_q05", "lift_q95",
                 "p_document")]
knitr::kable(held, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

Opened up lemma by lemma, the two lifts are of different kinds. That of
*god-true-lord* is one word: θεός carries almost all of the imputations'
excess over Sophocles, with πίστις, ἄγγελος and πιστός behind it, so the
judge's restorer names the god where Sophocles names him less. That of
*wrong-vengeance-err* is spread over the vocabulary of the play's matter:
χάρις, πόνος, δίκη, πάθος, ἑκών, αἰτέω, σῴζω and τιμωρός, favour and toil,
justice and suffering, the willing act, the rescue and the avenger, carry
the excess, while κέρδος, φίλτατος and τύχη fall below Sophocles' rate. The
judge keeps the lost verses on the wrong done and its requital. (Under the
smaller judge of the other set in the data, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, the one
lift that held against every baseline was *marriage-couch-bed*; here its
excess is carried by μόρος and θεά, two lemmata the clustering placed among
the marriage words, while the wedding words themselves, γάμος, λέχος, πόσις
and κόρη, sit at Sophocles' rate or below.)

```{r lemmata, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/hard_topic_lemmata_wrong-vengeance-err.png")
```

# Checks of the imputations' profile

Three checks that belong to the hard model's counts and are therefore in
this report only: how variable the topics are from document to document,
whether the imputations' lifts drift along the walk, and whether the chains
agree.

## How variable are the topics?

How much does a topic's share move from one document to the next, and does
that variability itself differ between topics? For every topic, the share
of a document's lemmata it takes is computed in every document, and its
standard deviation across documents is compared with the standard deviation
a multinomial of the same mean share and the set's mean length would
produce by sampling alone, $\sqrt{p(1-p)/N}$. Their ratio is the excess
variability: 1 means a topic varies no more than coin-tossing would, 2
means its real spread is twice that. The spread of these numbers across
topics is the "variance of the variances".

```{r variability}
# The share of every topic in every document, as a matrix
share_table <- function(documents) {
  shares <- matrix(0, nrow = length(documents), ncol = K)
  for (i in seq_along(documents)) {
    counts <- tabulate(match(documents[[i]], topic_names), nbins = K)
    shares[i, ] <- counts / length(documents[[i]])
  }
  shares
}

# Per topic: the mean share, its standard deviation across documents, the
# standard deviation sampling alone would give, and their ratio
topic_variability <- function(documents, label) {
  shares <- share_table(documents)
  mean_length <- mean(lengths(documents))
  share_mean <- colMeans(shares)
  share_sd <- apply(shares, 2, sd)
  sampling_sd <- sqrt(share_mean * (1 - share_mean) / mean_length)
  # a topic the set never uses has no spread to compare: its excess is NA
  excess <- ifelse(sampling_sd > 0, share_sd / sampling_sd, NA)
  data.frame(source = label, topic = topic_names, mean = share_mean,
             sd = share_sd, sampling_sd = sampling_sd, excess = excess)
}
variability <- rbind(topic_variability(sophocles_documents, "sophocles"),
                     topic_variability(imputation_documents, "imputations"))
for (column in c("mean", "sd", "sampling_sd", "excess")) {
  variability[[column]] <- round(variability[[column]], 4)
}

# One row per topic: Sophocles and the imputations side by side
sophocles_var <- filter(variability, source == "sophocles")
imputation_var <- filter(variability, source == "imputations")
side_by_side <- data.frame(topic = topic_names,
                           sophocles_mean = sophocles_var$mean,
                           sophocles_sd = sophocles_var$sd,
                           sophocles_excess = sophocles_var$excess,
                           imputation_mean = imputation_var$mean,
                           imputation_sd = imputation_var$sd,
                           imputation_excess = imputation_var$excess)
side_by_side <- arrange(side_by_side, desc(sophocles_excess))
knitr::kable(side_by_side, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r variability_summary, results = "asis"}
# The spread of the variability across topics, for Sophocles and the imputations
for (source_name in c("sophocles", "imputations")) {
  these <- filter(variability, source == source_name)
  cat(sprintf(paste("- **%s**: the between-document sd of a topic's share",
                    "ranges from %.3f to %.3f (median %.3f); its coefficient",
                    "of variation across topics is %.2f. The excess over",
                    "sampling ranges from %.2f to %.2f (median %.2f).\n"),
              source_name, min(these$sd), max(these$sd),
              median(these$sd), sd(these$sd) / mean(these$sd),
              min(these$excess, na.rm = TRUE),
              max(these$excess, na.rm = TRUE),
              median(these$excess, na.rm = TRUE)))
}
unused <- topic_names[colSums(share_table(imputation_documents)) == 0]
if (length(unused) > 0) {
  cat(sprintf(paste("- %s never occur%s in the imputations, so the rows of",
                    "that topic stay empty here and in the chain table.\n"),
              paste(unused, collapse = ", "),
              ifelse(length(unused) == 1, "s", "")))
}
```

```{r variability_plot, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(variability, aes(x = mean, y = sd, colour = source)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(aes(y = sampling_sd), linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = unname(okabe_ito[c("blue", "vermillion")])) +
  labs(x = "mean share of the topic", y = "sd of the share across documents",
       title = "Topic variability against its mean; dashed: sampling alone",
       colour = NULL)
```

## Where the walk went

A reviewer may object that the imputations' topics only reflect the region
of the restoration space that the chains happened to visit. Two checks
answer that.
First, does the lift of a topic drift as the walk proceeds? The snapshots are
grouped into windows of steps, every window is summarised like all the
imputations, and the slope of its lift against the step is the rate of change.
Second, do the sixteen chains agree over the steps they all cover? Each
chain's snapshots form a series of topic shares, and the
Gelman–Rubin $\hat R$ (BDA3 §11.4) compares the spread between chains with the
spread within them: $\hat R$ near 1 means a chain's share does not depend on
which chain it is.

```{r imputation_lemmata}
# One line per topic-bearing lemma of the walk, with its snapshot, chain
# and step
imputation_lemmata <- lemma_table(imputations, imputations$snapshot)
names(imputation_lemmata)[names(imputation_lemmata) == "group"] <- "snapshot"
imputation_row <- match(imputation_lemmata$snapshot, imputations$snapshot)
imputation_lemmata$chain_id <- imputations$chain_id[imputation_row]
imputation_lemmata$step <- imputations$iteration[imputation_row]
```

## Drift over the steps

```{r drift}
# The lift of every topic in each window of steps: the window's snapshots
# are its documents, compared with Sophocles exactly as all imputations are
lift_in_windows <- function(lemmata, breaks) {
  windows <- NULL
  for (i in seq_len(length(breaks) - 1)) {
    in_window <- lemmata$step > breaks[i] & lemmata$step <= breaks[i + 1]
    documents <- split(lemmata$topic[in_window], lemmata$snapshot[in_window])
    window_posterior <- summarise_documents(documents, baseline)
    window_rows <- data.frame(step = (breaks[i] + breaks[i + 1]) / 2,
                              topic = topic_names,
                              n_docs = window_posterior$n_docs,
                              lift = window_posterior$lift)
    windows <- rbind(windows, window_rows)
  }
  windows
}

# All chains over their whole run, in windows of 1000 steps; the windows
# beyond the shorter chains' last step hold only the eight longer chains
last_step <- max(imputation_lemmata$step)
drift <- lift_in_windows(imputation_lemmata, seq(0, last_step, by = 1000))

# The rate of change: the slope of lift against the step, per 1000 steps,
# fitted by least squares over the windows
slopes <- data.frame(topic = topic_names, slope_per_1000 = NA)
for (i in seq_len(K)) {
  topic_windows <- filter(drift, topic == topic_names[i])
  fit <- lm(lift ~ step, data = topic_windows)
  slopes$slope_per_1000[i] <- coef(fit)[2] * 1000
}
```

```{r drift_plot, fig.height = 4.5}
# The five topics with the steepest slopes are coloured; the rest are grey
steepest <- head(arrange(slopes, desc(abs(slope_per_1000))), 5)$topic
drift$shown <- ifelse(drift$topic %in% steepest, drift$topic, "other")
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = filter(drift, shown == "other"),
            aes(x = step, y = lift, group = topic), colour = "grey80") +
  geom_line(data = filter(drift, shown != "other"),
            aes(x = step, y = lift, colour = shown)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = unname(okabe_ito)) +
  labs(x = "step of the walk", y = "lift against Sophocles", colour = NULL,
       title = "Lift of every topic along the walk")
```

## Agreement between the chains

```{r rhat}
# The share of every topic in every snapshot, among its topic-bearing lemmata
# (a topic that no imputation uses still gets a column, of zeros)
counts <- table(imputation_lemmata$snapshot,
                factor(imputation_lemmata$topic, levels = topic_names))
shares <- counts / rowSums(counts)
snapshot_row <- match(rownames(counts), imputations$snapshot)
snapshot_chain <- imputations$chain_id[snapshot_row]
snapshot_step <- imputations$iteration[snapshot_row]

# The classic R-hat for chains of equal length: W is the mean within-chain
# variance, B the variance between the chain means scaled by the length
rhat <- function(x, chain) {
  chain_means <- tapply(x, chain, mean)
  chain_vars <- tapply(x, chain, var)
  n <- length(x) / length(chain_means)
  W <- mean(chain_vars)
  B <- n * var(chain_means)
  var_hat <- (n - 1) / n * W + B / n
  if (W == 0) return(NA)   # a share that never moves has no R-hat
  sqrt(var_hat / W)
}

# R-hat wants chains of equal length: the steps up to the shortest chain's
# last step, which every chain covers with the same number of snapshots
common_last <- min(tapply(snapshot_step, snapshot_chain, max))
common <- snapshot_step <= common_last
stopifnot(length(unique(table(snapshot_chain[common]))) == 1)
stability <- data.frame(topic = topic_names, rhat = NA,
                        chain_lift_q05 = NA, chain_lift_q95 = NA)
for (i in seq_len(K)) {
  x <- shares[common, i]
  chain <- snapshot_chain[common]
  stability$rhat[i] <- rhat(x, chain)
  # the lift of each chain on its own, against Sophocles' posterior mean
  chain_lifts <- tapply(x, chain, mean) / baseline$mean[i]
  stability$chain_lift_q05[i] <- quantile(chain_lifts, 0.05)
  stability$chain_lift_q95[i] <- quantile(chain_lifts, 0.95)
}

# One table: the lift of the walk, the drift and the chain agreement
stability$lift <- rows$lift[match(stability$topic, rows$topic)]
stability$slope_per_1000 <- slopes$slope_per_1000
stability <- stability[, c("topic", "lift", "slope_per_1000", "rhat",
                           "chain_lift_q05", "chain_lift_q95")]
stability <- arrange(stability, desc(rhat))
knitr::kable(stability, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r stability_summary, results = "asis"}
steepest_topic <- stability$topic[which.max(abs(stability$slope_per_1000))]
sentence <- paste("Over the whole run the median absolute slope is %.3f",
                  "lift units per 1000 steps; the steepest topic, %s, moves",
                  "%.3f per 1000 steps. The largest R-hat is %.2f (%s), the",
                  "next largest %.2f (%s).")
cat(sprintf(sentence, median(abs(stability$slope_per_1000)), steepest_topic,
            max(abs(stability$slope_per_1000)), stability$rhat[1],
            stability$topic[1], stability$rhat[2], stability$topic[2]), "\n")
```

```{r mixing, results = "asis"}
# How many topics the chains disagree on, and the spread of the chains' own
# lifts for the topic the report singles out
poorly_mixed <- sum(stability$rhat > 1.1, na.rm = TRUE)
with_rhat <- sum(!is.na(stability$rhat))
vengeance <- filter(stability, topic == "wrong-vengeance-err")
sentence <- paste("%d of the %d topics with an R-hat have one above 1.1: in",
                  "10,000 steps the chains have not mixed over the",
                  "restoration space, and a chain's share of a topic still",
                  "depends on which chain it is; whether that is the",
                  "start's doing is the next check's question. The lift of",
                  "wrong-vengeance-err runs from %.2f to %.2f over the",
                  "sixteen chains (their 5th and 95th percentiles), so the",
                  "pooled lift is an average over the starts rather than a",
                  "converged posterior; the resampling by chain in the",
                  "baseline comparisons above is what gives their intervals",
                  "their width.")
cat(sprintf(sentence, poorly_mixed, with_rhat, vengeance$chain_lift_q05,
            vengeance$chain_lift_q95), "\n")
```

## Unrelated starts

The sixteen chains start from Eric Cullhed's eight reconstructions, and
those are variants of one text: about nine per cent of the restored words
differ between any two of them. Their agreement is therefore agreement
between chains of one origin, and the poor mixing above may be the mark of
that origin or of the walk. A second set of eight chains under the same
judge, `chains_judge235_t4_spread`, tells the two apart. One chain keeps
Eric's text; the other seven start from late states of the sixteen chains
above, chosen one per source chain so that the eight starts are as far
apart in words as possible (`scripts/spread_starts.py` in the generation
repository: 96 to 100 per cent of the restored words differ between any
two starts, as between unrelated passages). Everything else is the same:
the judge, $1/T_{\text{judge}} = 4$, 10,000 steps, burn-in 300, a state
every ten steps. At the level of words the two sets end alike, with about
96 per cent of the restored words differing between two chains' final
states in either set, so what the comparison tests is the topic profile:
if a chain's topics depend on where it started, the spread set should
disagree more and its pooled lifts should move; if the walk forgets its
start, both sets should put the same topics into the passage.

```{r spread_set}
# The spread set, one document per snapshot, summarised like the report's
# set and compared with Sophocles
spread <- filter(untilted, restorer == "walk",
                 chain_set == "chains_judge235_t4_spread")
stopifnot(nrow(spread) > 0)
spread$chain_id <- paste(spread$chain_set, spread$chain)
spread$snapshot <- paste(spread$chain_id, spread$iteration)
spread_documents <- make_documents(spread, spread$snapshot)
spread_posterior <- summarise_documents(spread_documents, baseline)

# The share of every topic in every snapshot of the spread set, and the
# chain each snapshot belongs to; every chain has the same number of
# snapshots, so R-hat needs no trimming here
spread_lemmata <- lemma_table(spread, spread$snapshot)
names(spread_lemmata)[names(spread_lemmata) == "group"] <- "snapshot"
spread_counts <- table(spread_lemmata$snapshot,
                       factor(spread_lemmata$topic, levels = topic_names))
spread_shares <- spread_counts / rowSums(spread_counts)
spread_chain <- spread$chain_id[match(rownames(spread_counts),
                                      spread$snapshot)]
stopifnot(length(unique(table(spread_chain))) == 1)

# One row per topic: the lift and R-hat of each set, and the range of the
# spread set's eight chain lifts
starts <- data.frame(topic = topic_names,
                     lift_eric = rows$lift,
                     lift_spread = spread_posterior$lift,
                     lift_spread_q05 = spread_posterior$lift_q05,
                     lift_spread_q95 = spread_posterior$lift_q95,
                     rhat_eric = stability$rhat[match(topic_names,
                                                      stability$topic)],
                     rhat_spread = NA, chain_q05 = NA, chain_q95 = NA)
for (i in seq_len(K)) {
  x <- spread_shares[, i]
  starts$rhat_spread[i] <- rhat(x, spread_chain)
  chain_lifts <- tapply(x, spread_chain, mean) / baseline$mean[i]
  starts$chain_q05[i] <- quantile(chain_lifts, 0.05)
  starts$chain_q95[i] <- quantile(chain_lifts, 0.95)
}
starts <- arrange(starts, desc(rhat_eric))
knitr::kable(starts, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("topic", "lift, Eric's starts", "lift, spread",
                           "q05", "q95", "R-hat, Eric's starts",
                           "R-hat, spread", "chain q05", "chain q95"))
```

```{r spread_summary, results = "asis"}
# How alike the two sets' profiles are, how many topics each set's chains
# disagree on, and the topic the report singles out
agreement <- cor(log(starts$lift_eric), log(starts$lift_spread),
                 use = "complete.obs")
spread_raised <- starts$topic[spread_posterior$p_above[match(starts$topic,
                                 topic_names)] >= 0.9 &
                              starts$lift_spread >= 1.5]
both_raised <- intersect(rows$topic[rows$raised], spread_raised)
mixed_eric <- sum(starts$rhat_eric > 1.1, na.rm = TRUE)
mixed_spread <- sum(starts$rhat_spread > 1.1, na.rm = TRUE)
vengeance <- filter(starts, topic == "wrong-vengeance-err")
worst <- starts[which.max(starts$rhat_spread), ]
marriage <- filter(starts, topic == "marriage-couch-bed")
sentence <- paste("The log lifts of the two sets correlate at %.2f over the",
                  "%d topics. Raised in the report's set (lift at least 1.5",
                  "and a posterior probability of exceeding Sophocles of at",
                  "least 0.9) are %s; raised in the spread set are %s;",
                  "raised in both: %s. %d topics have an R-hat above 1.1",
                  "among the chains from Eric's starts and %d among the",
                  "chains from unrelated starts, so the chains disagree",
                  "about as much whether or not they share an origin: the",
                  "poor mixing is the walk's, not the starts', and 10,000",
                  "steps are not enough for one chain to represent the",
                  "posterior. The largest R-hat in the spread set, %.2f for",
                  "%s, is one chain's excess (its chains run from %.2f to",
                  "%.2f). Wrong-vengeance-err has lift %.2f in the spread",
                  "set, interval %.2f to %.2f, above Sophocles but under the",
                  "1.5 that counts as raised, and its eight chains run from",
                  "%.2f to %.2f; marriage-couch-bed falls to %.2f.")
cat(sprintf(sentence, agreement, sum(!is.na(starts$lift_spread)),
            paste(rows$topic[rows$raised], collapse = ", "),
            paste(spread_raised, collapse = ", "),
            if (length(both_raised)) paste(both_raised, collapse = ", ")
            else "none",
            mixed_eric, mixed_spread, worst$rhat_spread, worst$topic,
            worst$chain_q05, worst$chain_q95,
            vengeance$lift_spread, vengeance$lift_spread_q05,
            vengeance$lift_spread_q95, vengeance$chain_q05,
            vengeance$chain_q95, marriage$lift_spread), "\n")
```

## A third judge

The judge is the one part of the walk that is a language model's opinion,
so how much of the profile is the judge's? Beside the two Qwen sets the data
hold a pilot with a closed model as judge, Claude Sonnet 5.5 (the set
`chains_judge_claude-sonnet-5-5_t4`): eight chains from the same starts, the
same $1/T_{\text{judge}} = 4$ and the same prompt, each capped at 3.10 USD of
API calls, which bought about 1,500 steps. Three economies that the Qwen sets
did not have kept the cost down: a proposal that changed less than a tenth of
a verse's letters was dropped unjudged, burn-in ended once half the restored
letters differed from the start (between step 100 and 277), and a state was
recorded only when the restored letters had moved by a tenth since the last
record, about one state per 130 steps. The set is small, 387 documents, and
this report does not read it; it is here for the comparison.
`scripts/judge_comparison.py` computes the lifts of all three sets exactly as
in the baseline section above, and `results/hard/judge_behaviour.csv` (from
the walks' trajectories, `scripts/judge_behaviour.py` of the generation
repository) records what each judge returned.

```{r judges_behaviour}
behaviour <- read.csv("results/hard/judge_behaviour.csv", encoding = "UTF-8")
shown <- behaviour[, c("judge", "chains", "steps", "mean_abs_logodds",
                       "logodds_q50", "share_zero", "share_abs_ge_2",
                       "accepted_of_judged")]
names(shown) <- c("judge", "chains", "steps", "mean |log-odds|",
                  "median log-odds", "share zero", "share |log-odds| >= 2",
                  "accepted of judged")
knitr::kable(shown, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r judges_behaviour_summary, results = "asis"}
qwen <- filter(behaviour, judge == "Qwen3-235B")
sonnet <- filter(behaviour, judge == "Claude Sonnet 5.5")
sentence <- paste("The scales differ: a Qwen judge's log-odds is the",
                  "difference of two next-token logits, Sonnet's the log-odds",
                  "of a stated probability clamped to [0.01, 0.99], at most",
                  "4.6 in size. Even so the difference is one of kind. The",
                  "235B returns a mean absolute log-odds of %.1f and a median",
                  "of %.1f, a standing preference for the line already in",
                  "place, and the walk accepts %.0f %% of the proposals it",
                  "judges. Sonnet, asked at low effort and without thinking,",
                  "is close to indifferent: mean absolute log-odds %.2f,",
                  "exactly zero in %.0f %% of the steps (the same probability",
                  "in both orders), and %.0f %% of the judged proposals are",
                  "accepted. At the same $1/T_{\\text{judge}}$ it steers far",
                  "less; a sharper Claude judge would need thinking on or a",
                  "higher $1/T_{\\text{judge}}$.")
cat(sprintf(sentence, qwen$mean_abs_logodds, qwen$logodds_q50,
            100 * qwen$accepted_of_judged, sonnet$mean_abs_logodds,
            100 * sonnet$share_zero, 100 * sonnet$accepted_of_judged), "\n")
```

The lift of every topic against Sophocles under the three judges, for the
topics whose interval is off 1 under at least one of them; the intervals are
in `results/hard/judge_comparison.csv`.

```{r judges_lifts}
judges <- read.csv("results/hard/judge_comparison.csv", encoding = "UTF-8")
judges$off_one <- judges$lift_q05 > 1 | judges$lift_q95 < 1
soph <- filter(judges, comparison == "imputations vs sophocles")
judge_names <- c("Qwen3-235B", "Qwen2.5-72B", "Claude Sonnet 5.5")
# One column of lifts per judge, one row per topic
lifts <- data.frame(topic = sort(unique(soph$topic)))
for (name in judge_names) {
  these <- filter(soph, judge == name)
  lifts[[name]] <- these$lift[match(lifts$topic, these$topic)]
}
# A topic is shown when some judge's interval is off 1
off_any <- unique(soph$topic[soph$off_one])
lifts <- filter(lifts, topic %in% off_any)
lifts <- arrange(lifts, desc(.data[["Qwen3-235B"]]))
knitr::kable(lifts, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r judges_agreement, results = "asis"}
# How alike the three profiles are: the correlation of log lifts
# across all topics, and the topics raised under every judge
all_lifts <- data.frame(topic = sort(unique(soph$topic)))
for (name in judge_names) {
  these <- filter(soph, judge == name)
  all_lifts[[name]] <- these$lift[match(all_lifts$topic, these$topic)]
}
log_lifts <- log(all_lifts[, judge_names])
log_lifts[log_lifts == -Inf] <- NA
agreement <- cor(log_lifts, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
raised_by <- lapply(judge_names, function(name)
  soph$topic[soph$judge == name & soph$lift_q05 > 1])
raised_all <- Reduce(intersect, raised_by)
sonnet_only <- setdiff(raised_by[[3]], union(raised_by[[1]], raised_by[[2]]))
# Does wrong-vengeance-err hold against all three baselines under Sonnet?
vengeance_sonnet <- filter(judges, judge == "Claude Sonnet 5.5",
                           topic == "wrong-vengeance-err")
holds <- all(vengeance_sonnet$lift_q05 > 1)
sentence <- paste("The two Qwen profiles correlate at %.2f in log lift;",
                  "Sonnet's correlates with them at %.2f and %.2f. The judge",
                  "is a large part of the profile. What survives the change",
                  "of judge includes the topic the report singles out: the",
                  "topics with an interval above 1 against Sophocles under",
                  "all three judges are %s. Under Sonnet wrong-vengeance-err",
                  "%s against the other tragedians and against Classical",
                  "Attic too. Sonnet alone raises %s; the 72B's",
                  "marriage-couch-bed is at %.2f under Sonnet, below",
                  "Sophocles, and god-true-lord at %.2f with an interval",
                  "that covers 1.")
cat(sprintf(sentence, agreement["Qwen3-235B", "Qwen2.5-72B"],
            agreement["Claude Sonnet 5.5", "Qwen3-235B"],
            agreement["Claude Sonnet 5.5", "Qwen2.5-72B"],
            paste(raised_all, collapse = ", "),
            ifelse(holds, "also holds", "does not hold"),
            paste(sonnet_only, collapse = ", "),
            all_lifts[all_lifts$topic == "marriage-couch-bed",
                      "Claude Sonnet 5.5"],
            all_lifts[all_lifts$topic == "god-true-lord",
                      "Claude Sonnet 5.5"]), "\n")
```
